extraction.Name: William Walker
extraction.Refused/Protested: There was no protest made by Walker
extraction.Recorded patent: Walker never had patent recorded, ( lookup record in Brule Co)
extraction.Buyer: land was bought by J.Q.Anderson; Walker claims that he received $4700.00 for the half section that he paid $1500.00 on old debt and received $3200.00 in cash
extraction.Tax burden forced sale/Mortgage: Land was sold outright by Indian; some of the money was applied on an old debt, the debt was an old one that had run 4 years before the Indian had been told that he was to be given a patent
extraction.Occupation/Income: has supported himself by raising a small garden, working at odd jobs for the Gov't at farm station, and blacksmithing when he is able, has received some rations, that is his wife in winter
extraction.NOTES: Mental condition good, physical condition poor, financial condition poor; wife is dependent upon him; Still taxed; patent was delivered to Walker by Major McGlaughin; Walker was Indian police at time and received letter from Sup't Marble through Mr O'Shea farmer of the big bend district; at time this land was sold land of similar character was selling from $30. to 75. an acre; land was on the Missouri River bottom, 6 miles from the town of Chamberlain; document dated January 11th, 1929 | TASK 5 CAT_3 BACKFILL 2026-05-04 (patents database): Allotment 18 sourced from federal-register-app patents database (Christian's research, 2026-05-04).
